markdown_report:
## Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Industrial and Electronics have wrong-rank rates of 12.25% and 11.27%; negative lower-tail margins motivate improving difficult predictions. These training diagnostics do not establish validation performance. (2) Users report stale-interest recommendations and broadly relevant items they would defer. Immediate-next-choice supervision plausibly addresses both, but cannot establish compatibility, ownership, quantity needs, or current mood. (3) Embedding scores near 0.5 imply approximately zero mean cosine similarity, providing no evidence for collapse regularization. Unidentified-item skips must remain separate from explicit preference rejections.

**Literature insights.** (1) [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) already mixes terminal and random masking. Its reference generator produces ten random-mask copies plus one terminal copy; record proportions differ from supervised-token loss weights. (2) The [replicability study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07483) identifies training duration as a substantial confound. (3) [RSS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) motivates examining endpoint recency, but uses a different objective. (4) [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) and [AHNS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.05191) motivate negative coverage and controlled hardness without establishing transfer to this benchmark.

## Framework and candidate ideas

| Direction | Atomic experiment | Intended failure addressed |
|---|---|---|
| Prediction alignment | Increase terminal supervision on existing training windows | Historical relevance outweighs present choice |
| Historical coverage | Sample historical prefixes; vary endpoint recency separately | Recent specific interests receive insufficient emphasis |
| Candidate discrimination | Gradually introduce moderate hard negatives | Confusing candidates outrank positives |
| Item specificity | Jointly learn gated title/description embeddings | Broad resemblance obscures specific connections |

Scores are originality / potential / user alignment / model alignment / difficulty; difficulty 10 means hardest. Alignment scores describe hypotheses.

- **Terminal-supervision weighting: 2/6/7/7/3.** Originality + targeted weighting experiment; − established masking strategy. Potential + cheap foundation; − baseline may already suffice. User + addresses stale interests and deferred broad matches; − no compatibility guarantee. Model + targets next-choice separation; − gains uncertain. Difficulty + small sampler change; − requires exposure accounting.
- **Prefix-endpoint sampling: 3/6/7/6/4.** Originality + historical coverage within BERT4Rec; − related sampling precedents. Potential + tests recency; − dataset dependent. User + emphasizes recent specific interests; − recency can amplify noise. Model + adds prediction contexts; − changes context lengths. Difficulty + simple sampling; − several confounds.
- **Moderate-negative curriculum: 4/7/6/9/5.** Originality + controlled-hardness transfer; − established principle. Potential + targets lower-tail errors; − false negatives persist. User + distinguishes alternatives; − hardness does not encode usefulness. Model + targets wrong ranks; − sampled-candidate overfitting. Difficulty + unchanged architecture; − mining cost.
- **Gated text embeddings: 4/6/8/6/6.** Originality + compliant joint text learning; − established pattern. Potential + represents specific attributes; − sparse supervision. User + captures identifiers/artists; − ownership remains unknown. Model + may distinguish similar IDs; − unverified. Difficulty + single network; − tokenization and predictor changes.

## Selected experiment

At 0% progress, select **increased terminal-supervision weighting**, narrowing the original prefix-terminal proposal to avoid changing endpoint sampling simultaneously. It targets stale interests and broadly plausible but deferrable recommendations, plus weak positive–negative separation. Preserve baseline window/user sampling; alternate terminal-only and baseline random-mask batches 1:1, averaging supervised-token losses within each batch. Terminal examples replace the existing window’s final item with MASK. Historical-prefix sampling remains a separate follow-up: choose a training target, discard its suffix, and mask it; uniform endpoints change both historical coverage and context lengths.

Compare against the corrected baseline with architecture, loss, optimizer, negatives and checkpoint rule fixed. Report updates, supervised targets, visible-context lengths and GPU seconds: equal updates do not ensure equal supervision or compute. Equal-target and equal-time comparisons are secondary controls only if the shared budget permits; they must retain the epoch/update caps.

Keep one checkpoint/category, routing, seeds 0/42, maximum 200 epochs × 200 batches, left padding and appended-mask inference. Use final-nonpadding readout. Select by pinned macro validation HR@10: 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, seed 42. Report category results and all selection attempts. [Sampled HR](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) does not establish full-catalog quality. If paired hit vectors are available, report a stratified paired percentile bootstrap interval, 10,000 replicates, seed 42; it excludes training variability and adaptive-selection bias. Treat gains as exploratory, freeze configuration before held-out evaluation, and preserve separate qualitative checks for immediate choice and explicit incompatibility. No gains are claimed.

idea.description: Increase terminal-only supervision within the corrected BERT4Rec baseline while preserving its existing training-window and user-sampling distributions. Alternate terminal-only and baseline random-mask batches in one jointly trained model per category. Defer historical-prefix endpoint sampling to a separate experiment.
idea.motivation: User feedback identifies stale historical interests and broadly plausible recommendations users would defer. Greater terminal supervision may improve immediate-choice ranking, addressing those two failures, while negative lower-tail margins in Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics motivate measuring difficult positive–negative separation. These are hypotheses; neither the diagnostics nor prior literature establish validation gains or equipment compatibility.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve the supplied backbone, scoring function, optimizer, negative sampling, loss and data splits. First record the corrected baseline's actual masking policy, window sampling, batch size and checkpoint rule; the supplied report does not contain enough baseline code to specify these numerically. Terminal masking is established BERT4Rec practice, so the intervention is its frequency and effective objective weight. Use the baseline's existing sampled training windows, requiring at least two nonpadding items. For terminal batches, replace the window's last item with the reserved mask token and supervise only that position. For random batches, retain the corrected baseline's masking policy and ensure supervised item identities are hidden rather than shifted into bidirectional context. Alternate batches 1:1 and average each batch loss over its supervised targets; this produces equal batch-objective weighting rather than equal numbers of targets. Log actual terminal supervision because random masking can also select terminal positions. Keep user/window sampling and pre-mask window lengths identical between comparison arms; report visible-context distributions because masking itself changes available context. The earlier proposal to sample a historical target uniformly, remove its suffix and mask it remains a separate follow-up, with an explicit minimum target index of one and a separately specified endpoint distribution. Do not attribute that bundled change solely to inference alignment. Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], four-category routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution and artifacts beneath the trial directory. All training, diagnostics and failed trials count toward 43,200 GPU seconds. Report equal-update results and exposure/compute totals; undertake equal-supervised-target or equal-time controls only within the same caps and budget, without claiming all resources are simultaneously matched. Use the unchanged baseline checkpoint rule and disclose every evaluated configuration/checkpoint. Retain exactly one independently trained checkpoint per category; compare trials without fusing their predictions. The predictor writer must emit an architecture-consistent working/predict.py with appended-mask inference, truncating history to MAXLEN-1 before appending MASK. Find the greatest nonpadding index, never count-1. Keep log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), host ModelView interfaces, DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Probe only genuinely hidden targets from the family-specific B x L batches; exclude padding/mask IDs from candidate diagnostics and document negative construction. Mark unavailable category breakdowns unavailable. Only histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions may be used; ratings, review text, item categories/prices/stores, ownership and simulator traits are unavailable. Preserve twenty training-user full-catalog recommendation probes, five/category, and separate unidentified-item skips from explicit mismatches. Sampled validation HR@10 and full-catalog qualitative feedback answer different questions. If host per-user hit vectors are available, bootstrap paired user differences separately within categories with 10,000 percentile replicates and seed 42, recomputing the equally weighted macro difference; otherwise omit the interval. The interval is conditional on fitted models and fixed candidates and does not correct adaptive selection. No validation improvement is claimed before host evaluation.
idea.pseudocode:
set_preprocessing_seed(0)
set_training_seed(42)
# Run comparison configurations sequentially within the shared GPU budget.
# Each evaluated predictor loads one checkpoint per category; never fuse runs.
for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    model, optimizer = corrected_baseline_BERT4Rec(category)
    for epoch in range(MAX_EPOCHS_AT_MOST_200):
        for step in range(200):
            windows = baseline_sample_training_windows()
            if step % 2 == 0:
                examples = []
                for window in windows:
                    # Use the existing window endpoint; do not resample prefixes.
                    assert len(window) >= 2
                    target = window[-1]
                    sequence = left_pad(window[:-1] + [MASK], MAXLEN)
                    position = greatest_nonpadding_index(sequence)
                    examples.append((sequence, position, target))
            else:
                examples = corrected_baseline_random_masked_examples(windows)
            assert_supervised_targets_hidden(examples)
            features = model.log2feats(examples.sequence)
            loss = baseline_loss_at_supervised_positions(features, examples).mean()
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            log_updates_targets_context_lengths_and_gpu_time()
        unchanged_baseline_validation_and_checkpoint_rule()
    save_one_selected_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor(category)
# Inference:
# sequence = left_pad(history[-(MAXLEN-1):] + [MASK], MAXLEN)
# features = model.log2feats(sequence)
# scores = model.predict_score(features[greatest_nonpadding_index(sequence)], candidates)
# Follow the host's existing tensor/batch interfaces.
# Deferred prefix experiment only:
# t = sample_training_target_index(history, minimum_index=1)
# sequence = left_pad(history[:t][-(MAXLEN-1):] + [MASK], MAXLEN)
# target = history[t]; never include history[t+1:].

originality.positive: A controlled change in effective terminal-supervision weighting is a focused experiment tied to the observed immediate-choice failures.
originality.negative: BERT4Rec already includes terminal-only examples; neither terminal masking nor its inference-alignment rationale is new.

future_potential.positive: A low-cost controlled experiment can establish a reliable foundation before introducing endpoint recency, text features or harder negatives.
future_potential.negative: Benefits may saturate if the corrected baseline already supplies sufficient terminal supervision, and this intervention cannot establish compatibility or present needs.

code_difficulty.positive: The network and inference architecture remain unchanged; implementation primarily affects training-example construction and loss accounting.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable comparison requires auditing existing masking, exposure counts, padding, hidden targets, diagnostic validity and checkpoint selection.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item learning for sequential recommendation.
Includes terminal-only masking to improve alignment with appended-mask inference.
The reference generator mixes random-mask copies with terminal-only copies, and its loss averages over supervised targets.
limitations: Terminal masking is established prior art, limiting the proposed experiment's novelty.
Record mixture proportions do not directly specify terminal loss weight.
The one-mask ablation does not isolate terminal versus interior supervision under matched updates, targets, context and compute.
Its results do not establish the best masking mixture for this fixed Amazon benchmark.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec reference training-example generator
contributions: Provides implementation evidence for random-mask copies, terminal-only examples and deterministic window generation.
limitations: The supplied corrected host baseline may use a different implementation and must be characterized independently.
Original implementation settings do not establish an optimal mixture for this benchmark.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec reference loss implementation
contributions: Shows supervised-target loss averaging, explaining why example proportions and objective weights differ.
limitations: Its weighting must not be assumed to match the corrected host baseline without checking the supplied implementation.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec replicability study
contributions: Identifies training duration as a substantial factor in reproducing BERT4Rec performance.
limitations: Does not establish that longer training or a particular masking mixture improves this Amazon benchmark.
Its findings motivate compute accounting without authorizing changes to the task's fixed training caps.

related_work.title: Recency-based Sampling of Sequences
contributions: Investigates target recency under controlled training duration.
Motivates separating endpoint recency from masking-position effects.
limitations: Uses target-set prediction rather than historical-prefix terminal masking.
Does not provide a direct controlled BERT4Rec terminal-versus-interior ablation.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Examines sampled-BCE overconfidence and motivates improved negative coverage and objective calibration.
limitations: Uses a different backbone; only objective-design motivation transfers here.
Does not establish gains for the proposed BERT4Rec masking-policy experiment.

related_work.title: Adaptive Hardness Negative Sampling for Collaborative Filtering
contributions: Motivates adaptive negative hardness to manage problems associated with fixed hardness.
limitations: Evidence concerns collaborative filtering rather than this masked sequential benchmark.
Hardness alone does not establish compatibility or eliminate false negatives.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics and reverse model rankings.
limitations: Does not invalidate the pinned benchmark as the required selection objective.
Additional repetitions cannot generally remove sampled-metric bias.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents bootstrap interval methods and paired resampling.
limitations: The proposed category-stratified paired macro bootstrap requires an explicit adaptation.
User resampling conditional on fixed models and candidates excludes training variability, negative-resampling variability and adaptive-selection bias.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated model selection can overfit finite validation data.
limitations: Does not quantify selection bias for these particular trials.
Disclosure and conditional bootstrap intervals do not remove adaptive-selection bias.
